component: Single-domain local federation revision, digest and trusted-time persistence
constraints: Offline one-row metadata, protected local filesystem and cooperating processes. Explicit initialization, no implicit repair/reset, exact domain and snapshot pin; no identified target or hard-real-time SLA.

Persist valid deny-all independently of bundle success; atomic read-check-write, nondecreasing time/revision and same-revision digest consistency. Preserve existing policy v1 disk format and rejection behavior.
alternatives: Native SQLite transactions through Python sqlite3, Rust rusqlite, or C#/F# Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.
Atomic JSON replacement with OS locking, file/directory synchronization and explicit recovery protocol.
Erlang/Elixir OTP Mnesia transactions and local disk tables.
LMDB native transaction API; documentation retrieval failed again during this review, so no unsupported negative capability claim is made.
rationale: KEEP SQLite and the Python binding after reviewing the existing persistence component: SQLite provides atomic local updates and writer serialization without introducing a custom journal. BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires the write transaction before reading floors; timeout zero rejects contention.

Python invokes the existing exact-byte validator in the same process. Rust and .NET can provide sound SQLite bindings but do not by themselves add stronger snapshot acceptance, rollback detection or cross-file atomicity. No measured target constraint demonstrates a material benefit from replacing this boundary.

Mnesia is a credible runtime outside the component language and supports transactions; its broader database/distribution model does not resolve the identified whole-store-restore limitation. Atomic replacement needs a separate concurrent read/check/write locking and crash protocol.

Share the reviewed transaction machinery using fixed subclass SQL profiles, preserving policy disk bytes. Add a separate federation application ID/schema and immutable metadata type rather than treating federation as a policy. Decisions are constraint-based, not based on installed tools, familiarity or rewrite cost.
limits: No alternative executable prototype or benchmark was run; no latency, resource superiority or universally best technology claim. LMDB source retrieval failure limits the comparison.

Atomic-commit properties depend on SQLite VFS/filesystem/hardware assumptions. Commit-failure injection is not physical power-loss qualification. Native/real-time targets require independent selection and evidence.

Whole database restore can lower floors. No independent rollback anchor, authenticated storage, encryption, trust enrollment or coordinated policy/federation transaction. All authority/qualification flags remain false.
